subject: SLO metrics access & verification playbook request
messages:
From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@acme.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>; procurement@acme.com
Cc: Chris Lee <chris.legal@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 8 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLO measurement details + customer metrics access

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the demo earlier — the product looks promising for our chat-heavy customer support flows. Our procurement team has a few follow-up questions about how you measure and expose SLOs so we can complete the vendor risk questionnaire:

1) How do you define "availability" vs "request success" for the hosted API?
2) What latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99) do you guarantee and over what evaluation window?
3) What telemetry will we be able to see directly (metrics/logs/dashboards)? Can we get read-only Grafana access or raw Prometheus metrics?
4) If there is an exception (planned maintenance or capacity incident), what is your exception approval process and how long are exceptions logged?

We're trying to tie answers back to our security/compliance questionnaire. Could you send a short playbook or examples we can attach to the packet? If you prefer, loop in your SRE/SE for technical details.

Cheers,
Sophie Turner
Sourcing Manager, Acme Corp

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>; Chris Lee <chris.legal@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 8 May 2027 17:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLO measurement details + customer metrics access

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear list. I attached a short playbook (slo-metrics-playbook.pdf) and an example set of PromQL queries (example-promql-queries.txt) that should map directly to your questionnaire fields. Summary here so you have the highlights immediately: 

- Availability / Success: We treat a request as "successful" when the inference pipeline returns a 2xx response within the configured request timeout and the response passes our output-validation hook (no truncated/invalid payload). Availability SLO = percentage of successful requests across 1-minute windows over a rolling 30-day period.

- Latency SLOs: Default published targets (hosted SKU) — p50 < 120ms, p95 < 320ms, p99 < 1.2s for short-run text generation (<=512 tokens). Targets are measured on completed requests (successful responses) and reported as rolling percentiles over a 30-day window; we can provide alternate measurement windows for contract language.

- Telemetry & access: Customers may choose one of the following access models:
  * Read-only Grafana invite (managed account) — fastest; we provide pre-built dashboards for availability, per-model latency histograms, error rates, and quota burn.
  * Metrics export (push) to your Prometheus/SignalFx using a short-lived tenant token — you ingest our metrics into your monitoring.
  * Aggregated CSV/JSON delivery for procurement/legal if you need artifacts rather than live access.

- Alerting & monitoring: We run synthetic probes (every 20s) across regions + real traffic aggregation. Alerts are generated on burn-rate (service level burn) and error-rate spikes. We provide the alert rules and sample PromQL in the attached file.

- Exception path: Planned maintenance: 72-hour notice + maintenance window published. Emergency exceptions (capacity or provider impact) are logged and a formal exception ticket is created; exceptions older than 1 year are archived, and all exception records are retained for 13 months by default (we can extend retention under contract).

Next steps: I can provision read-only Grafana access for your SREs and share the invite token if you confirm the email list. Marissa will follow up on onboarding details and our standard SLA appendix.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Attachments: slo-metrics-playbook.pdf (overview + sample queries), example-promql-queries.txt (promql examples for p95/p99/error-rate)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@acme.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 8 May 2027 18:31:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLO measurement details + customer metrics access

Hi Sophie — quick note from the SRE / onboarding side.

If you want live visibility we typically do the Grafana read-only route for procurement review. Practical details:
- We create a team-level read-only account scoped to your org domain (or to specific users). The invite file (grafana-readonly-invite.txt) contains an enrollment link and TTL for the token.
- Dashboards included: Availability (1m windows), Request latency (histograms + p50/p95/p99), Error taxonomy (4xx/5xx/validation-errors), KV cache hit ratio, and regional traffic split.
- Prometheus metrics we expose: redwood_request_total, redwood_request_success_total, redwood_response_latency_seconds_bucket, redwood_request_error{reason}. The example queries demonstrate how to compute SLO burn rates.

A couple of pragmatic notes:
- We measure SLOs on the customer tenant-id level. If you use our Dedicated offering, the absolute latency targets are tighter and are measured across the same 30-day rolling window.
- If procurement needs screenshots or exported CSVs for legal, we can schedule an export job for the relevant 30-day window once we have the signing date.

Karthik, can you add the escalation / exception checklist here? Sophie — if you can share the SRE addresses for the two people who should get Grafana access, I’ll send the invite today.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 9 May 2027 11:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLO measurement details + customer metrics access

Sophie — adding the exception workflow details you asked about: 

- Incident classification: We classify incidents that affect SLOs into three levels (minor, major, critical) based on user impact and duration.
- Exception approvals: Planned exceptions (maintenance) are coordinated through the Account team and require a single SLO-exception form + approval from the Reliability manager. Emergency exceptions are auto-logged and flagged for post-incident review; contractual exceptions (e.g., extended maintenance window) require a written amendment.
- Measurement specifics (for contract): SLOs are calculated as the ratio of successful 1-minute windows over the rolling evaluation window (default 30d). For latency percentiles we use weighted aggregation across regions, and percentile windows are computed on completed requests only. We include sample PromQL for computing the error budget burn rate in the attached example-promql-queries.txt.
- RCA and evidence: For any SLO breach we provide an RCA within 5 business days and raw metric exports on request (delivery via secure link).

If that all works, Rachel — please provision Grafana readonly and attach the invite to the hubspot deal (ACME-12345). Sophie — once your SREs confirm emails I’ll lock down the dashboards and add a short runbook to the playbook.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
